results.content:
## Where Kokonut UI stops short

 React and Next.js only, no Vue or vanilla HTML/CSS/JS output
 Runs on Motion, not GSAP, so there's no timeline sequencing, ScrollTrigger-style scroll control, or SVG/MotionPath tooling built in
 CLI install has shipped real friction: multiple GitHub issues report the `npx shadcn add` command aborting with an "unsafe file path" registry error, and one issue notes the copy-paste install command pointed at the wrong URL
 Components come from an open community catalog rather than commissioned client work, so depth and polish vary component to component
 The Pro tier is a fixed one-time catalog, not an ongoing production system, there's no equivalent of a documented, uniform tuning contract across every component

Limitations as of September 2026. [...] Does Kokonut UI's CLI install actually work reliably?
:   Mostly, but not always cleanly. The GitHub repo has had multiple reported issues where the shadcn CLI install command (`npx shadcn add ...`) aborted with an "unsafe file path" registry error, plus at least one issue where the copy-paste install command pointed to the wrong URL. Those were community-reported and the repo shows zero open issues as of 2026-09, but it's worth testing the exact install command for the component you want before committing to it.

## When Annnimate is the better pick

Annnimate is the better pick when the animation has to do real work. Kokonut runs on Motion, so scroll choreography, pinned sections and timeline sequencing aren't in its toolkit, and its components come from an open catalog rather than commissioned projects, so polish varies piece to piece. Annnimate ships every component on GSAP with the same documented attributes, reduced-motion and keyboard behavior, and delivers Vue and plain HTML alongside React from one source.

## How to install

Kokonut UI is a shadcn/ui registry, so every component arrives as source in your repo, with its dependencies installed.

1. AI agentA

   Name a component, or describe what you need. Your agent finds it in the registry and installs it with its dependencies.
2. shadcn CLIB

   Name the component. The shadcn CLI writes the file and installs what it needs.
3. RegistryC

   Add the namespace to components.json once, then use the short names everywhere.
